concerns.text: Task T012 (naive_generator) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T008 (Generate Ground Truth Subset) to define the 'clean state' baseline for drift injection. The task description states 'Crucially, this subset must be generated... to serve as the ground truth', creating a hidden data-flow dependency that violates the [P] tag and the parallel execution model implied for Phase 2.

T014 (Implement Ground Truth Validation Logic) and T015 (Run Ground Truth Validation) are placed within User Story 1 implementation but depend on T008 (Generate Ground Truth Subset) from Phase 2. While T008 is in Phase 2, the dependency chain T008 -> T014 -> T015 -> T016 (Drift Score) is not explicitly serialized in the 'Dependencies & Execution Order' section, risking T016 running before T015 validates the CV pipeline accuracy (FR-007).

Tasks T020a, T020b, and T020c are all marked [P] (parallel-safe) but the description explicitly states 'Must be implemented first', 'Depends on T020a', and 'Depends on T020b'. They modify the same file (`code/hybrid_controller.py`) and represent sequential logic steps. Marking them [P] is a semantic violation of the parallel-safe contract and will cause race conditions or merge conflicts if executed in parallel.

T023 (Statistical Analysis) depends on T017 (Baseline Run) and T022 (Hybrid Run). The 'Dependencies & Execution Order' section lists T017 as a prerequisite for T023, but fails to explicitly list T022 as a prerequisite for T023, despite T023 requiring `data/hybrid_scores.json` generated by T022. This missing dependency link breaks the producer-consumer flow for the final statistical output.

The 'Checkpoint' at the end of Phase 3 states 'User Story 1 should be fully functional', but T015 (Run Ground Truth Validation) is a blocking gate for the validity of the drift score (FR-007). The checkpoint implies success without explicitly confirming the T015 validation pass, creating a semantic gap in the 'independently-shippable' claim for US1.
